lessons.title: Component State Management with React Hooks & Reducers
overview: In modern scalable React 19 architectures, managing high-velocity client updates without cascading re-renders requires distinguishing between localized component state and compound domain state. In this lesson, Rohit Sen dissects the trade-offs between atomic state hooks (useState) and deterministic action reducers (useReducer).

We examine practical implementation models for state lifting, action payload serialization, preventing memory leaks in asynchronous dispatchers, and pairing reducers with React 19 transition primitives for non-blocking UI rendering.

takeaways.title: Deterministic Reducer Contracts
takeaways.desc: Keep reducers pure with no asynchronous side effects. Route API triggers via customized hooks or middleware.

takeaways.title: Granular Context Splitting
takeaways.desc: Separate State Context and Dispatch Context to safeguard non-dependent consumers from unwanted renders.

takeaways.title: Non-blocking with useTransition
takeaways.desc: Wrap heavyweight state transitions so critical user gestures (e.g. typing, clicking) remain 60fps responsive.

takeaways.title: Production Debugging with Redux DevTools
takeaways.desc: Integrate native browser telemetry for time-travel debugging across complex multi-step modal workflows.
